question: What is the main goal of good nutrition for someone living with HIV?

options.B: To support the immune system and enhance treatment
options.C: To prevent passing the virus to others
options.D: To guarantee permanent weight gain for everyone

explanation: Spot on! Good nutrition gives your body the strength to fight off infections and helps HIV medications work much better.

question: Why does poor nutrition make HIV progress faster?

options.A: It causes instant resistance to antibiotics
options.B: It destroys the outer shell of the virus
options.C: It stops the liver from handling water
options.D: It further weakens the body's natural defenses

explanation: You got it! Without proper nutrients, the immune system simply doesn't have the fuel it needs to keep the virus in check.

question: By about how much should a patient with symptomatic HIV who is losing weight increase their daily calories?
explanation: That's right! When the body is fighting active symptoms and dropping weight, it needs about 30% more energy to recover and maintain strength.

question: An HIV patient is losing muscle mass rapidly. Which nutrient should the nurse focus on most during counseling?
explanation: Correct! Protein is the ultimate body-builder nutrient needed to repair wasted muscles and keep the body strong.

question: Why do vitamin and mineral shortages happen so easily in people living with HIV?

options.A: Due to poor intake, malabsorption, and inflammation
options.B: Because the virus uses up all carbohydrates
options.C: Because antiretroviral drugs destroy vitamins instantly
options.D: Because they drink too much clean water

explanation: Spot on! Gut inflammation and eating less food mean the body struggles to absorb the vital nutrients it needs.

question: What is the danger of giving very high megadoses of a single vitamin to an HIV patient?

options.B: It can cause toxicity or worsen viral replication
options.C: It completely replaces the need for water
options.D: It will cure the infection instantly

explanation: Correct! Just because a vitamin is natural doesn't mean more is always better. Megadoses can actually harm the body or help the virus multiply.

question: How often should a nurse check a stable HIV patient's weight to catch any nutritional drops early?

options.D: Only when they have a fever

explanation: You got it! Checking weight regularly helps you spot trouble before it turns into severe malnutrition or muscle wasting.

question: What is the quickest and most practical way for a nurse to check what a patient has eaten recently during a busy clinic day?

options.A: Admitting the patient for a week
options.D: Ordering a full metabolic blood panel

explanation: Spot on! Asking 'What did you eat and drink yesterday?' gives you a fast, reliable picture of their current intake.

question: What is the best eating strategy for an HIV patient dealing with severe nausea?

options.A: Avoiding all fluids for twelve hours
options.B: Eating three large oily meals daily

explanation: Correct! Small, gentle meals keep the stomach from feeling overloaded and help keep nausea at bay.

question: Why are fiber and low-fat diets important for long-term HIV care?

options.A: To manage metabolic complications like high cholesterol
options.B: To stop the patient from catching colds
options.C: To increase red blood cell counts
options.D: To directly kill the virus in the blood

explanation: Spot on! Long-term ARV use can affect how the body handles fats and sugars, making heart-healthy food choices extra important.

question: Why must certain antiretroviral drugs be taken alongside food?

options.A: To stop the patient from feeling hungry at night
options.C: To reduce stomach irritation and improve drug absorption
options.D: To destroy the outer tablet coating instantly

explanation: You nailed it! Some meds are much easier on the stomach and work better when taken with a meal or snack.

question: What is a major risk of mixing herbal products with HIV medications without asking a doctor?

options.A: They turn the medicine into harmless sugar water
options.B: They always cure the infection faster
options.C: They have zero effect on drugs
options.D: They can dangerously lower drug levels in the blood

explanation: Correct! Some herbs mess with liver enzymes, clearing out life-saving medications too quickly and making them less effective.

question: Why is food safety especially critical for patients with weakened immune systems?

options.A: Their bodies struggle to fight off foodborne infections
options.B: Bad water changes their skin color
options.C: Dirty food automatically stops medicines from working
options.D: Uncooked meat increases muscle mass too fast

explanation: Spot on! An immune system that is down cannot easily fight off germs from bad food, leading to serious illness.

question: Which of these practices is NOT safe for an HIV patient?

options.A: Drinking unboiled surface water during travel
options.C: Washing raw fruits and veggies with clean water

explanation: You got it! Unboiled water is packed with germs that cause severe diarrhea, which can quickly worsen malnutrition.

question: Why should nurses recommend locally available, affordable foods during nutritional counseling?

options.A: Local foods completely replace the need for drugs
options.B: Expensive imported foods have zero nutrients
options.C: Patients refuse to eat anything foreign
options.D: It ensures the dietary advice is realistic and sustainable

explanation: Spot on! Good nursing advice must fit the patient's real life and pocket so they can actually follow it.

question: A patient says they cannot afford the expensive imported supplements prescribed elsewhere. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the patient to the hospital management
options.B: Tell the patient to stop eating altogether
options.C: Tell them to borrow money to buy the brand
options.D: Help the patient find affordable local whole-food alternatives

explanation: Brilliant! As a nurse, you bridge the gap by showing patients how to get great nutrition using what is easily available around them.
